nodes.description: mapping(address=>uint256) private _balances holding token balances of each account
mapping(string=>uint256) private _transactions used as replay-protection registry of consumed withdraw ids
uint private maxSupply = 10000000000 * 10**18, hard cap used by internalWithdraw
uint256 private _totalSupply total amount of minted tokens
address accessAuthority = 0xA04885E222c1FF34e8E87601EE6e314166b35f33, signer authorised to approve withdrawals
uint256 private _status reentrancy guard flag inherited from ReentrancyGuard
public nonReentrant withdraw(string id, uint256 numberOfTokens, bytes signature) delegating to internalWithdraw
external nonReentrant batchWithdraw(string[] ids, uint256[] numberOfTokens, bytes[] signatures) looping over internalWithdraw
private internalWithdraw(string id, uint256 numberOfTokens, bytes signature) validating signature, id uniqueness and max supply then minting
private view isWithdrawAuthorised(string id, uint256 numberOfTokens, bytes signature) verifying ECDSA signature against accessAuthority
private view withdrawAccessor(string id, uint256 numberOfTokens) building the signed message from id, amount, contract address and msg.sender
external onlyOwner nonReentrant transferBalance() sending the whole contract balance with a low-level call
external onlyOwner setAccessAuthority(address addr) replacing the withdrawal signer
external onlyOwner setMaxSupply(uint newMaxSupply) replacing the hard supply cap
internal _mint(address account, uint256 amount) increasing _totalSupply and _balances
internal _burn(address account, uint256 amount) decreasing _balances and _totalSupply
msg.sender, attacker-controlled caller used as mint recipient and as message component / refund receiver
(bool success,) = msg.sender.call{value: address(this).balance}("") low-level value transfer executed before state finalisation

edges.reason: withdraw() unconditionally delegates to internalWithdraw()
batchWithdraw() calls internalWithdraw() repeatedly inside an unbounded loop
msg.sender is passed as the mint recipient inside internalWithdraw -> _mint(msg.sender, numberOfTokens)
internalWithdraw() requires isWithdrawAuthorised(...) before minting, making signature verification the access gate
internalWithdraw() calls _mint(msg.sender, numberOfTokens) after the uniqueness and cap checks
internalWithdraw() writes _transactions[id] = numberOfTokens after requiring _transactions[id] == 0
isWithdrawAuthorised() builds the digest through withdrawAccessor() before ecrecover
withdrawAccessor() concatenates msg.sender into the signed payload, binding the signature to the caller
isWithdrawAuthorised() compares the ECDSA-recovered address to accessAuthority
_mint() increases the recipient entry of _balances using SafeMath add
_mint() increases _totalSupply using SafeMath add, checked against maxSupply in internalWithdraw
_burn() decreases _balances[account] using SafeMath sub
_burn() decreases _totalSupply using SafeMath sub
setAccessAuthority() overwrites the signer address used to authorise withdrawals
setMaxSupply() overwrites the hard cap that limits minting
transferBalance() is gated by onlyOwner which compares _owner to _msgSender()
transferBalance() forwards the whole balance through a low-level call to msg.sender
the low-level value transfer hands control to msg.sender, which can re-enter owner functions before the call returns
msg.sender is the callee of the balance transfer and therefore fully controls execution flow
the nonReentrant modifier on withdraw() reads and writes _status around the external state changes
the nonReentrant modifier on batchWithdraw() reads and writes _status around the loop
